topic.title: Identifiers
topic.description: Rules for naming variables, methods, and classes

sections.title: 🎯 What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Ever wondered how programmers name their variables, methods, or classes? Let's dive into the rules of identifiers!

• What identifiers are and why they matter
• The dos and don'ts of naming things in Java
• How to make your code readable and professional

sections.title: 💡 Concept Explanation
sections.content:
Imagine you're labeling boxes in a warehouse. Each box needs a unique, clear name so workers know what's inside. Identifiers are like those labels for your code!

In Java, identifiers are names you give to:
• Variables (like `age` or `totalPrice`)
• Methods (like `calculateTax()`)
• Classes (like `Student` or `BankAccount`)

**Rules to follow:**
• Must start with a letter (a-z, A-Z), underscore (`_`), or dollar sign (`$`)
• Can include letters, digits, underscores, or dollar signs after the first character
• Cannot be a Java keyword (like `int`, `class`, or `public`)
• Case-sensitive (`age` ≠ `Age` ≠ `AGE`)

sections.title: ⚡ Key Points
points: ✓ Identifiers are names for variables, methods, and classes
✓ Must start with a letter, `_`, or `$` (no digits!)
✓ Can include letters, digits, `_`, or `$` after the first character

sections.title: 🔥 Tips & Mistakes
dos: Follow Java naming conventions (camelCase for variables/methods, PascalCase for classes)
donts: Don’t use spaces or special characters (e.g., `total price` or `total-price`)
sections.protip: Avoid `$` in names—it’s reserved for generated code (like in IDEs).

sections.title: 🌍 Real World Use
sections.content: Where are identifiers used in real apps?

examples.how: Use identifiers like `accountBalance`, `transactionDate`, and `Customer` class to organize financial data.
Identifiers like `userName`, `postContent`, and `LikeButton` class help manage user interactions.

problem.description:
Which of these are valid Java identifiers? Fix the invalid ones:
1. `2ndAttempt`
2. `user_name`
3. `class`
4. `totalAmount`
5. `void`
6. `$price`
hints: Check if it starts with a letter, `_`, or `$`.
Make sure it’s not a Java keyword.
Remember: No spaces or special characters!
problem.explanation: Valid identifiers must follow the rules: start with a letter/underscore/dollar sign, avoid keywords, and use only allowed characters.

sections.title: 📝 Summary
points: 📌 Identifiers are names for variables, methods, and classes
📌 Must start with a letter, `_`, or `$` (no digits or keywords!)
📌 Practice naming things clearly and consistently
📌 Ready to learn about variables next!
